crop.notes: The main headline is missing. On the page the column opens 'PRIZE-RING RULES. Why Fights for Championships Must Be Governed by Them.' above the deck that starts the clipping. The body and Allen's statement are complete.

ocr.notes: Mostly right, with scattered errors ('gem Allen' for 'Tom Allen', 'Jem in correspondence' for 'I am in correspondence', 'Qmaha' for 'Omaha').

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported Tom Allen's word that Jem Smith, with whom he was corresponding, would fight Sullivan only under London prize-ring rules with bare fists, and not east of Omaha.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Tuesday, January 4, 1887', page 5. Most of the item is Tom Kelly's view on championships; Allen's statement is the last paragraph.

facts.fact: Allen said he was in correspondence with English champion Jem Smith, who told him he would not fight Sullivan east of Omaha and only under London prize-ring rules with bare fists
facts.quote: I am in correspondence with Smith and he tells me that he will not fight Sullivan east of Omaha. He doesn't think he would be given a fair show in any city in the Eastern country and if he fights he's got to fight fair.

facts.fact: Allen said a Smith-Sullivan fight would be for the championship and no championship could be won under any rules but the London prize-ring rules
facts.quote: If Jem Smith of England fights Sullivan, he must fight him under London prize-ring rules, with bare fists, of course. A fight between Smith and Sullivan would be for the championship and no championship could be won under any other rules. No gloves can be used at all.

notes: Recrop to include the 'PRIZE-RING RULES' headline if wanted.
